name: Alfama
description: Lisbon's oldest quarter, on the slope below São Jorge castle. Largely survived the 1755 earthquake; narrow cobbled lanes, traditional fado houses, and Tagus views.

name: Mouraria
description: Multicultural quarter on the north side of São Jorge castle, historically the Moorish district after the Christian reconquest of 1147. Widely considered the birthplace of fado.

name: Graça
description: Hilltop residential neighbourhood above Alfama, anchored by the Graça and Senhora do Monte viewpoints. Quieter than the central quarters, with neighbourhood cafés and the National Pantheon nearby.

name: Baixa
description: The grid of Pombaline streets rebuilt after the 1755 earthquake, running from Rossio down to the river at Praça do Comércio. Pedestrianised main axes and the Santa Justa lift connecting up to Chiado.

name: Chiado
description: Cultural quarter on the hill above Baixa — the São Carlos opera, the National Theatre, historic cafés like A Brasileira, and the main bookshops. Where most first-time visitors orient themselves.

name: Bairro Alto
description: Grid of narrow streets above Chiado that goes quiet by day and turns into the city's late-night drinking quarter, with bars spilling out onto the pavement until well after midnight.

name: Príncipe Real
description: 19th-century neighbourhood above Bairro Alto, built around the central garden square. Concept stores in the Embaixada palace, independent restaurants, design hotels.

name: Cais do Sodré
description: Riverside district at the western end of Baixa. Home to the Time Out Market in the Mercado da Ribeira, the Cascais train terminus, and the Pink Street nightlife strip on Rua Nova do Carvalho.

name: Alcântara
description: Riverside district under the 25 de Abril bridge, west of the centre. Home to LX Factory, a hub of restaurants, studios, and weekend markets in converted industrial warehouses.

name: Lapa
description: Quiet 19th-century neighbourhood west of the centre, home to many of Lisbon's embassies and to the Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga overlooking the river.

name: Belém
description: Riverside district at the western edge of the city, anchored by the Jerónimos Monastery, the Belém Tower, the MAAT museum, and the Pastéis de Belém bakery. Reachable from the centre by tram 15 or train.

name: Avenidas Novas
description: Early-20th-century planned extension north of the centre along Avenida da República. Business district with the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum and adjoining garden.

name: Marvila
description: Post-industrial district along the river east of the centre, repurposed into a creative quarter — galleries, breweries, design studios, riverside warehouses.

name: Parque das Nações
description: Eastern riverside district built for Expo '98, around Santiago Calatrava's Oriente station. Anchored by the Oceanário, the Vasco da Gama tower and shopping centre, and the cable car along the Tagus.
